learning_outcomes.text: Students will gain advanced experience working with game environments and among game developers of various professions (graphics, game designers).

syllabus_topics: Use of C++ in the Unreal Engine environment
Linking Blueprint code with C++ code
Comparison of game environments Unity, Unreal and others
Organization of a team of game developers
Basic means of development of these types of games
Implementation of game mechanics such as dialogues, inventories, skill trees, crafting, game tasks, interactive tutorials
Advanced player interaction with the game, the use of touch input devices, gamepads, game steering wheels, joysticks, devices for tracking the player's head position and gaze direction
Solving specific problems when developing your own game project
Using external means for creating shaders, 3d models and animation
Customization and export of games for PC, mobile and TV-connected platforms
assessment_rules: The indicative evaluation scale is: A 90%, B 80%, C 70%, D 60%, E 50%. The scale of assessment is 100% preliminary, 0% final.
bibliography: 3D game engine design : A practical approach to Real-Time computer graphics / David H. Eberly. Amsterdam: Elsevier, 2007
Real-time rendering / Tomas Akenine - Möller , Eric Haines, Naty Hoffman. Wellesley : AK Peters, 2008
institution: Univerzita Komenského v Bratislave (Comenius University Bratislava)
degree: Bachelor Applied Informatics (1-AIN), Faculty of Mathematics, Physics and Informatics
